claims.claim: The campaign features an open world layout with natural-feeling environments, though some find traversal and map activities sparse or frustrating.

citations.review_text:
Its a great edition to the Halo franchise! 
I truly enjoy the open world aspect of the game and multi player feels more like it went back to its roots than a couple other games.

I hear people are deriding this game. I don't know about multiplayer but open world feels natural for the Halo series, and the main missions are a return to form. The villains are pretty good, better than any of the previous games'. The gameplay is fluid and feels like old times. I've gotten several hours out of the campaign and feel that it's been worth my investment. I really like this direction for the series, and I hope later installments build on it without repeating it.

As with many open world shooters, the respawning enemies in areas I've already cleared is annoying, and collectables are always frustrating when it's not clear where they all are. I don't like having to double back to pick up upgrades.

I do wish air vehicles were available earlier in the game, there are some areas that are a huge pain in the butt to get to.

I love being able to summon vehicles, tanks, and guns that I like from the FOB's instead of having to hunt down the vehicle I want.

I cam back to this game years after release and finally beat the campaign. My initial stop was because I got so frustrated with an open world map where it seemed there was just so little actually going on in it. Transversal was just a pain in the butt and not fun.

I also hated how this game, particularly in the end, turned into a bullet-sponge snooze fest.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the open world as repetitive, empty, bland, and generic, featuring the same repetitive activities like capturing bases and destroying outposts.

citations.review_text:
Hey kiddo, Handsome Jack here... and I just played Halo Infinite, and honestly? It's pretty good. Not amazing, not terrible, just good. You get to play as Master Chief, drive around a giant alien ring, shoot aliens, blow things up, and swing around with a grappling hook like a very angry green Spider-Man. And I'll admit, that's pretty fun.

The gunplay is still fantastic, the weapons feel great, and driving a Warthog into a group of unsuspecting aliens never gets old. The open world is fun for a while too, but eventually you start noticing that you're doing the same things over and over again. Capture this base, destroy that outpost, rescue these guys, shoot those guys. At some point you're just driving around thinking, “Wait, haven't I already done this?”

The story is decent, the characters are fine, and Master Chief is still Master Chief, so obviously there's some quality control happening somewhere. But it also feels like there was a much bigger game hiding in here that never quite showed up. There's plenty to enjoy, but not enough that made me sit there thinking, “Wow, I NEED to keep playing this.”

So yeah, kiddo, 7/10. It's fun, it looks good, the shooting feels great, and occasionally you get to do something ridiculously cool. But it's not exactly the second coming of gaming. It's more like the gaming equivalent of a perfectly acceptable sandwich. You'll eat it, you'll enjoy it, and then five minutes later you'll wonder why you didn't order something better.

Still, not bad.

And that's coming from me, so you know I'm being incredibly generous.
It's easy to see why halo infinite failed, it's just so empty.

The only good thing I can say is that the core gameplay is fun and responsive. On the other hand:
- bland and generic open world
- coop borderline unplayable due to bugs
- a story not worthy of that name

The worst Halo game.

(Realistically this is a more mixed review but ill overall put it negative ig)

Unlike H4 & 5, Infinite is actually fun to play! Great core gameplay here and the grappleshot is a lot of fun to use. The return to the classic art style, tone and music is a breath of fresh air, and the game distancing itself from the awful narrative of H5 and retconning a lot of it is also totally welcome. Unfortunately the actual story this game tells is very underwhelming, with no compelling stakes or interesting villains. The linear missions are also incredibly generic, and lack variety and have almost no set pieces. The open world is fun to run around and vibe in, but i wouldve traded it all for a more traditional Halo experience with a more well rounded story and missions.

claims.claim: Players experience technical performance issues such as stuttering and frame drops during matches.

citations.review_text:
Decided to get back into the multiplayer with Campaign Evolved releasing. I do love the game, the cosmetics etc but my god they need to sort the stuttering/performance issues. 
I have tried in game settings, turning off game bar, AMD specific settings and nothing seems to be a permanent solution. Some games will play smooth and really makes the game enjoyable. 
Others have constant stuttering, frame drops and I can't see any warnings about connection issues. But I never have any other issues like this with other games I play. 
I recommend it if you are a genuine halo fan, not if you just want another shooter to play.

Just plain fun if you load up custom games with some friends. Have been getting random lag spikes that I haven't been getting before either on windows or before the update that added the impossible gauntlet mode.

While I've only played for 160 hrs on steam, I have over 520 hours as of writing this (xbox console and xbox app on windows) . The online multiplayer used to be really fun, but now only the sweats play so it would be best to avoid online matchmaking. However, if you can convince some friends to hop on, it's a blast.

claims.claim: The menus and user interface are described as buggy, choppy, and poorly performing.

citations.review_text:
Don't be fooled by the steam records. I have over 3k hours on this garbage.

Ill lay it out simple and straight for you. 

When this came out 5 years ago, that was it. That was the actual final straw for the Halo franchise. Not Reach, not 5, not MCC, this one right here. And they failed, miserably. Now the only people who play this game are the losers like me who have been playing for the last 20 years. Or anyone new and unfortunate enough to accidentally stumble upon it.

-Constant disconnection issues over the years, still there.
-Terribly sweaty and toxic community trying to relive their primes. Check.
-Constant desync and wall/angle/bullet issues over the years. Still not fixed.

You know what does work? The store. Buying cosmetics. Putting your credit/debit card info into the Microsoft platform. That sure works great. But the game doesn't.

-The UI has been buggy and choppy since release
-The developers have been opaque and unhelpful
-$550,000,000 budget to make a half baked cosmetic app.

I could go on and on about the issues this game has. I can't stress enough how many issues this game has had and still has. But I'm sure you get the point now.

All I can do is beg, plead and hope that the parents of the children who are spending money on this game, and the fully developed adults who keep shoveling money into this dumpster fire, please stop. Please stop. Please.

They don't deserve your money. They don't deserve another car, or another boat or another house. They have turned modern gaming into a cash grab that has sucked the soul out of many of our favorite titles, not just Halo.

Please, for the love of the future of gaming. Stop buying cosmetics on these games. All you're doing is reinforcing the terrible systems they have in place, and will stay in place indefinitely if we don't do something. Speak with your wallet. If you want the big heads to listen, talk with money. 

Parents of children who play: wake up, take a stand, teach your child that bad people …

A pretty solid multiplayer experience hampered by perhaps the worst performing menus and UI that I have ever seen in a videogame. When you're actually playing though, its good fun and there's a ton of different PvE and PvP gamemodes - all for free. Its still got a pretty active playerbase at a mix of skill levels. If you're interested in playing for cosmetics, you can drop £10 of in-game currency and buy the several battle passes that actually refund that money on completion (not all of them do, so check), and you'll get a fair few from those - otherwise, pretty much everything on the store is a massive rip off in terms of price, so buyer beware.

claims.claim: Cosmetics and in-store items feature high price tags, and progression requires a heavy grind.

citations.review_text:
It's a good game but not as good as the Bungie Halos. Will go more into depth but the TL;DR: Game gets a 7/10.

Campaign is fun and story is good, best 343 has made at least.
Multiplayer feels like Halo multiplayer and Forge/Custom maps and game modes are great.
Downside: Progression/customization is slower and harder than it needs to be. I mean, a real grindfest. You don't feel like an old Halo, BF, or COD where you levelld and won stuff. Spartan points and levels come slow and a lot of items are locked behind a payable battle pass.

My opinion? People are either hungry for live service games (lots of complaints when this game came out, very quickly, about a lack of updates/content drought.) which just feels entitled because Halo CE-3 weren't that. You bought the game, had campaign and multiplayer, and that was it. Period. But nowadays people think if it isn't getting constant and massive updates the game is bad. Sad, tbh.

Alright, for the real stuff:

Campaign! It's fine, the story is interesting, the characters like Joy and the pilot are great. The villains? Not so much.  Atriox is really weird disappearing right at the beginning, the Banished don't really have a lot of interest/motive, and gameplay wise the AI is really slow, dumb, and easy to handle. 

The collectibles, the side stories (such as with the Spartan 4s and the Zeta Halo battle you miss), are really cool if you're into lore and the Halo universe. 

Gameplay: It's fine. Just fine. It feels like Halo, even with new additions like the grapple hook, and the upgrading your suit doesn't feel bad either. But it isn't great. Like I said, the AI is too simple, the gunplay doesn't feel as impactful as other games, your allies aren't all that useful or important (the outpost system could have been WAY better, at least more polished), and that makes the game not so memorable overall.

Multiplayer: This is where you get Halo. Anyone can jump in or out, there's a bunch of game modes, at the time of writing there…

A pretty solid multiplayer experience hampered by perhaps the worst performing menus and UI that I have ever seen in a videogame. When you're actually playing though, its good fun and there's a ton of different PvE and PvP gamemodes - all for free. Its still got a pretty active playerbase at a mix of skill levels. If you're interested in playing for cosmetics, you can drop £10 of in-game currency and buy the several battle passes that actually refund that money on completion (not all of them do, so check), and you'll get a fair few from those - otherwise, pretty much everything on the store is a massive rip off in terms of price, so buyer beware.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the campaign lacks planned downloadable content continuations since planned updates were cancelled.

citations.review_text:
ok so, the multiplayer is fun. Pretty solid honestly. Lots of free content but lots more paid content (cosmetics)
Its a bummer. Live service games are anti consumer. Gunplay feels good and is fun. 

The story mode was ok. Its more halo but it sucks that they arent continuing this story, this master chief is done well. I like the weapon

I suppose now that it's done, it's about time to review this game. A few months after launch, this would be a negative review. It took 2 years for this game to be in a healthy state when it comes to having enough maps, gamemodes, forge, etc. That 1-2 year drought still lingers with me as how bad post launch support can be for a game.

Now though, it has enough content even if they cut support last year. The gunplay is good, the weapon sandbox is great and well balanced imo, the ttk is long as it has been for the majority of this franchise, the movement is ok but lacks fluid momentum that I prefer. The artstyle is good and feels like halo (imo 2 anniversary has the best artstyle for halo within it's campaign). The overall multiplayer gameplay loop feels like an updated version of 3 with armor pickups.

TLDR: The game is fun and is Halo

I have not played it's campaign since the game launched nearly 5 years ago. I remember the sandbox was really fun. I liked the story more than 5 and CE. I like the pilot and this iteration of Chief's character. It's a shame that the planned campaign dlc got axed and we have not gotten a new game that continues and expands with what Infinite's story left. I still don't know what the ♥♥♥♥ an endless is. Atriox should have been this game's main villain and showing him alive at the end when he'd been missing since the opening cutscene is a dissapointing tease. I hope we get a proper sequel someday and 343/halo studios don't scrap the prior entry's story like they have done 3 times in a row from 4 to 5 to infinite.
